meta.title: Decommunisation
meta.question: Should former communists be held to account?
meta.measure: Average support for decommunisation and lustration, from 0 (opposed) to 10 (strongly in favour)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on decommunisation and lustration, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Agree or disagree: communism (the communist party) should be prohibited

Own position, 0-10: people who held high posts in the PRL state apparatus and former SB agents should now be barred from high public office (0) vs it is not worth looking into office-holders' communist-era past, what matters is what they do now (10)
items.notes: PGSW 1997, 2001, 2005, 2007. The 2005 second-wave panel re-interview (decomm_self_010_w2) is not used.

items.wording: Former high-ranking communists should be removed from influential posts (strongly agree ... strongly disagree)
Should lustration now be carried out in Poland, that is, checking whether people in important state posts collaborated with the communist security service? (definitely yes ... definitely not)
items.notes: CBOS 1997-12, 1999-09, 2002-03, 2005-02. In 1997-12 the file has two variables with this label (both asked of everyone); the first is used.

items.wording: Former communists should not be allowed (in politics/public life) (strongly agree ... strongly disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1998 only; one statement in a battery on democratic principles.

items.wording: Does lustration rather improve or worsen the climate of political life in Poland?
items.notes: CBOS 1999-09 and 2002-03. The 2006-09 question about lustration under the proposed new rules is not used.

items.wording: Own position, 0-10: the communist nomenklatura should be banned from responsible state functions (0) vs should have the same rights as everyone else (10)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study (single survey); PGSW's decommunisation scale with the nomenklatura wording.

items.wording: Is lustration and the disclosure of the IPN files, to settle accounts with the past, one of the most important problems to be solved without delay, or a substitute issue serving only political games?
Should we still be settling accounts with the PRL, since it has not been dealt with sufficiently, or should we end the reckoning and leave the period to historians?
